Yes! You can generally bring a 20,000 mAh power bank on a flight in the United States, provided it is rated at no more than 100 watt-hours (Wh). The important rule is that it must go in your carry-on bag, not checked luggage. FAA official guidance

What you need to know

Carry-on bag: Yes

Power banks rated up to 100 Wh are generally permitted. A typical 20,000 mAh power bank is approximately 74 Wh.

Checked luggage: No

Spare lithium-ion batteries and power banks must remain in the aircraft cabin.

Protect the battery

Prevent damage and short circuits. If your carry-on is gate-checked, remove the power bank and keep it with you in the cabin.

Source: FAA — Airline Passengers and Batteries and FAA — Lithium Batteries.
